# An extracted vault verifies against its own trust anchor, so a fabricated one
# verifies as happily as the real thing. An attacker needs no key of ours to build
# one: our recipients are public (sesam.yml), so they can tell a user with our
# public key into their own repo, seal whatever they like at our path, and push
# that .sesam as a branch. The incoming vault is therefore pinned to this repo
# before anything is decrypted out of it.

sesam-repo admin real.txt ours.txt evil.txt

cp $TMPDIR/real.txt app.env
exec sesam add app.env --group admin
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'add app.env'

# The attacker's own repo, with a secret at the same path. ADMIN_PUBKEY stands in
# for what they would scrape out of our committed sesam.yml.
mkdir $TMPDIR/evil
cd $TMPDIR/evil
exec git init
exec git config user.email test@sesam.dev
exec git config user.name 'Sesam Test'
env SESAM_ID=$BOB_KEY
exec sesam init --user mallory
exec sesam tell --user admin --recipient $ADMIN_PUBKEY --group admin
cp $TMPDIR/evil.txt app.env
exec sesam add app.env --group admin
cd $WORK
env SESAM_ID=$ADMIN_KEY

# Push the fabricated vault as a branch.
exec git checkout -b evil
exec rm -r .sesam
exec cp -r $TMPDIR/evil/.sesam .sesam
cp $TMPDIR/evil/sesam.yml sesam.yml
exec git add -A
exec git commit --no-verify -m 'evil: fabricated vault'

# Our own change to the same secret, so git has to invoke the driver.
exec git checkout master
cp $TMPDIR/ours.txt app.env
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'ours: rotate'

! exec git merge evil
stderr 'belongs to a different repository'
stderr 'refusing to merge it'

# Refused before decrypting, so our plaintext was never touched.
exec cat app.env
stdout 'OURS'
! stdout 'PWNED'

-- real.txt --
REAL
-- ours.txt --
OURS
-- evil.txt --
PWNED
